problems.problem_text: In triangle ABC, AB = 6 cm, AC = 8 cm and angle BAC = 60°. Find BC using the cosine rule.
problems.solution: Using cosine rule: a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A. BC² = 6² + 8² - 2(6)(8)cos60° = 36 + 64 - 96(0.5) = 100 - 48 = 52. BC = √52 = 7.21 cm.

problems.problem_text: In triangle PQR, PQ = 5 cm, PR = 7 cm and QR = 8 cm. Find the angle at P.
A triangle has sides of length 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. Use the cosine rule to find the largest angle.
problems.solution: Largest side is 6 cm opposite largest angle. cos θ = (4² + 5² - 6²)/(2×4×5) = (16+25-36)/40 = 5/40 = 0.125. θ = cos⁻¹(0.125) = 82.8°.

problems.problem_text: Find the side length a in a triangle where b = 9 cm, c = 7 cm and angle A = 48°.
A ship sails 12 km east, then 15 km on a bearing of 060°. How far is it from its starting point?
problems.solution: The angle between the two paths is 180° - 60° = 120°. Using cosine rule: d² = 12² + 15² - 2(12)(15)cos120° = 144 + 225 - 360(-0.5) = 369 + 180 = 549. d = √549 = 23.4 km.

problems.problem_text: Triangle ABC has AB = 11 cm, AC = 9 cm and angle BAC = 72°. Find BC and the angle at B.
An isosceles triangle has equal sides 10 cm and base 12 cm. Find the apex angle.
A garden triangular lawn has sides 8 m, 11 m and 14 m. Find the smallest angle of the triangle.
In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, AC = 11 cm and angle B = 38°. Find all possible values of side BC.
problems.solution: Using sine rule: sin C / 8 = sin 38° / 11 → sin C = 8 sin 38° / 11 = 0.447. C = 26.6° or 153.4°. If C = 26.6°: A = 180-38-26.6 = 115.4°, BC² = 11²+8²-2(11)(8)cos115.4° = 121+64-176(-0.431) = 185+75.9 = 260.9, BC = 16.2 cm. If C = 153.4°: A = 180-38-153.4 = -11.4°, impossible. Wait, this is cosine rule problem. Using cosine rule with alternate approach: BC² = AB²+AC²-2(AB)(AC)cos A. Without angle A, use substitution.

problems.problem_text: A quadrilateral ABCD has AB = 5 cm, BC = 7 cm, CD = 9 cm, DA = 6 cm and diagonal AC = 8 cm. Find angle BCD.
A right square-based pyramid has base side 6 cm and slant height 10 cm. Find the angle between a slant edge and the base plane.
problems.solution: Half of diagonal of base = 3√2 = 4.24 cm. Slant edge = 10 cm. Height: h² = 10² - 4.24² = 100 - 18.0 = 82.0. h = 9.06 cm. cos θ = 4.24/10 = 0.424. θ = 64.9°.

problems.problem_text: A plane flies 200 km on bearing 050°, then 150 km on bearing 140°. Find its distance and bearing from the starting point.
problems.solution: Angle between paths = 140° - 50° = 90°. Using Pythagoras: d² = 200² + 150² = 40000 + 22500 = 62500. d = 250 km. Bearing: θ = tan⁻¹(150/200) = 36.9°. Final bearing = 50° + 36.9° = 86.9°.

problems.problem_text: Prove the cosine rule: a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A for any triangle ABC.
problems.solution: Place triangle with A at origin, AB along x-axis. Coordinates: A(0,0), B(c,0), C(b cos A, b sin A). Then a² = (b cos A - c)² + (b sin A)² = b² cos²A - 2bc cos A + c² + b² sin²A = b²(cos²A + sin²A) + c² - 2bc cos A = b² + c² - 2bc cos A.

problems.problem_text: A triangle has two sides of length 8 cm and 12 cm. The included angle varies. Find the maximum possible length of the third side.
problems.solution: By cosine rule: c² = 8² + 12² - 2(8)(12)cosθ = 64 + 144 - 192 cosθ = 208 - 192 cosθ. c is maximized when cosθ is minimized (-1 at θ = 180°).c²_max = 208 - 192(-1) = 400. c_max = 20 cm.

problems.problem_text: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, CD = 10 cm, DA = 7 cm and diagonal BD = 9 cm. Find angle ABC.
A triangle has sides of length a, b and a+b. Show that the angle opposite the longest side must be greater than 120°.
problems.solution: Longest side is (a+b). By cosine rule: cos C = (a² + b² - (a+b)²)/(2ab) = (a² + b² - a² - 2ab - b²)/(2ab) = -2ab/(2ab) = -1. So cos C = -1 and C = 180°. But a triangle with sides a, b, a+b is degenerate (collinear). For a non-degenerate triangle, a+b > c and C > 120° only when... Actually cos C = -1 means the triangle is degenerate. For a proper triangle, C approaches 180° but never reaches it, so angle > 120°.
